healthcareSystem: Government-run public healthcare with very limited capacity. National Referral Hospital in Honiara is the main facility. Provincial hospitals provide basic care. Outer islands have clinics with minimal staffing and supplies. Healthcare infrastructure is severely underdeveloped.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is extremely limited. The National Referral Hospital in Honiara is the only facility with reasonable capacity but is often overcrowded and under-resourced. Provincial hospitals are basic. Outer islands have aid posts with minimal supplies. Specialist care is virtually nonexistent. Medical evacuation to Australia is standard for serious cases. English is an official language but Pijin is more commonly spoken.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Honiara open 8am-5pm weekdays. Very few pharmacies outside the capital. Hospital pharmacies may have limited stock.
pharmacyTips: Bring all necessary medications from home. Pharmacy stock is very limited and unreliable. Medications may be expired or counterfeit in informal outlets. Only purchase from hospital pharmacies or licensed pharmacies in Honiara. Insect repellent with DEET is essential for malaria prevention.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is inconsistent. Some medications available over the counter that would require prescriptions elsewhere. However, stock is very limited so availability is the main issue. Bring all prescription medications from home.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Carry doctor's letter and keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal. Do not bring any cannabis products.

restrictedMeds.name: Amphetamines/stimulants
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly prohibited. Carry documentation for ADHD medications.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter for all prescription medications. Keep medicines in original packaging. Bring a comprehensive travel medical kit as pharmacies may not have what you need.

travelInsurance.tips: Absolutely essential. Medical evacuation to Australia is very expensive and may be the only option for serious conditions. Ensure policy covers medical evacuation with no sub-limits. Diving and adventure sports coverage is important. Remote island travel adds significant risk.

required: Yellow Fever (only if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
recommended: Rabies (for extended stays or animal contact)
vaccinations.notes: Malaria is endemic throughout the Solomon Islands, including Honiara. Antimalarial prophylaxis is strongly recommended. Consult a travel medicine specialist before departure. Dengue fever is also present.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink anywhere in the Solomon Islands. Always use bottled, boiled, or purified water. Even in Honiara, water treatment is unreliable. Bring water purification tablets or a portable filter for outer island travel. Avoid ice unless made from purified water.
foodSafetyTips: Exercise caution with all food. Eat freshly cooked, hot food. Avoid raw vegetables and salads unless you can verify they were washed with purified water. Fresh tropical fruit you peel yourself is safe. Fish and root vegetables (taro, sweet potato) are staples. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera poisoning risk in certain areas.
medicalTourismNote: Not a medical tourism destination. Solomon Islands is a destination for diving, WWII history, and cultural tourism. Travelers should be fully self-sufficient for medical needs.
sources: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Smartraveller)
Solomon Islands Ministry of Health and Medical Services
metaDescription: Health guide for Solomon Islands: malaria prevention, unsafe water, hospitals in Honiara, medical evacuation, and insurance.

hospitals.name: National Referral Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in the country. Emergency department available but often overcrowded. Limited specialist equipment. English spoken by doctors, Pijin by most staff.

hospitals.name: Good Samaritan Hospital (Helena Goldie Hospital)
hospitals.notes: Church-run hospital near popular dive sites. Basic care only. Useful for Western Province visitors.

hospitals.name: Gizo Hospital
hospitals.notes: Provincial hospital. Basic emergency care. Near popular dive and island-hopping areas.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. Basic dental services at the National Referral Hospital in Honiara. No private dental clinics of international standard.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is extremely basic. Only emergency extractions and basic procedures available. No cosmetic or advanced dentistry.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Go to the National Referral Hospital dental clinic in Honiara. Outside Honiara, dental care is essentially unavailable.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Virtually none. Some counseling through NGOs and church organizations.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited. The National Referral Hospital has a small psychiatric unit. For any serious mental health needs, evacuation may be necessary.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is virtually nonexistent. Roads are unpaved outside Honiara. Most buildings lack wheelchair access. The country is extremely challenging for travelers with mobility impairments.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: National Referral Hospital has minimal accessibility features. Most health facilities are not wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are rough and unsealed. Inter-island travel is by small boats and light aircraft, neither of which are accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: The Solomon Islands is extremely challenging for travelers with mobility impairments. Honiara is the most navigable area but still very limited. Contact tour operators well in advance to discuss specific needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Some health facilities may request masks.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at National Referral Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been lifted. Health infrastructure remains limited regardless of COVID status.

insuranceClaimProcess: Pay upfront for all medical care. Facilities may not provide detailed receipts so request itemized documentation. Keep all records. File claims with your insurer after returning home. Communication challenges may require patience when obtaining documentation.

commonCosts.note: Costs are approximate and relatively low but facilities are basic. Solomon Islands Dollar (SBD) is local currency. Few facilities accept credit cards.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Suva, Fiji or Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is extremely important given the limited healthcare. Evacuation to Australia is the standard for serious cases. Outer island evacuations add complexity and cost. Helicopter or charter plane may be needed from remote areas.
